ops.entry: WHEN auditing filesystem recovery discovery DO compare the names discovery trusts, the names legitimate producers emit, and the names write authorization reserves; check every path component a write can implicitly create, not just its final component.
ops.why: The review exposed successive mismatches across producer, discovery and gate, including a reserved name reachable through implicit parent creation. This reusable boundary check displaces the narrower credential-sweep reminder.

ops.entry: WHEN a terminal review uncovers a finding adjacent to a named class DO route it to the ruling tier with the class-defining evidence, impact, recovery cost, parity with previously ruled routes, and which links were executed versus inferred; do not assume a class-specific remedy applies.
ops.why: The terminal ruling distinguished the closed discovery contract from an availability-only perimeter gap. Explicit routing evidence is more useful than forcing independent reviewers to share a severity.

originals.original: WHEN a dispatch names specific files to check DO also grep the full diff for secrets/credentials, not only the named files — docs, config, and workflow changes carry credential-shaped strings too, and a narrowed sweep misses them.

WHEN your finding's mechanism is independently matched by another reviewer's finding at the same site, from a different lens, DO name the convergence explicitly — it is stronger evidence of a real gap than either alone — and reconcile severity down to the shared value, never average or escalate.
